title: Document model
body: A document is one JSON file in the sources folder. The id is the file name without the extension: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen. Folder names follow the same rules, and the reserved Windows names are rejected.

The built-in schema requires only `title`. The reserved fields are `title`, `kind`, `status`, `parent`, `order`, `tags`, `body`, `notes`, `hidden`, `docIgnore` and `$comments`. Every other field is free and holds prose. `order` is a number that sorts a document among its siblings.
The checks are listed in [[rules]] and the generated pages in [[rendering]].
typing: Every document has a `kind`, and the folder of schemas holds `<kind>.json` for it. A document without a kind, or with a kind that has no schema, is reported as DOC109, a core rule that cannot be switched off.

A kind schema must set a boolean `additionalProperties` at the top level: `true` makes the kind flexible, `false` makes it strict. Without it the schema does not load and docc exits with code 2. For a strict kind docc checks the field names itself: the allowed names are the reserved fields, the top-level `properties` and the `properties` of the top-level `allOf` branches and of local `$ref` targets; names under `if` and `then` are not counted. An unknown field is DOC106 with the message `unknown field X` and a suggestion of the closest allowed name.
The kind schema sees the whole document, reserved fields included, so it can require `parent` or limit the values of `status`.

`"x-docc-target": ["goal"]` on a property, `parent` included, limits the kinds of the documents its references point to; a reference to another kind is DOC214. `"x-docc-covered": true` at the top level of a kind schema means that every visible document of the kind needs a `docc:` tag in code, otherwise DOC403 warns when `trace.scan` is set.
references: Inside any string, `[[id]]` links to a document and `[[id#field]]` links to one of its fields. Both are checked like `parent`. A reference in the text is the link: it joins two documents in the graph and puts the source under Referenced by on the target page; there is no separate list of links. References inside `notes` are checked but give no reachability. Code blocks and inline code are ignored.
A long text is an array of paragraphs, one per line of the file. The rules are applied to each element on its own.
A reference can name a section inside a field, `[[id#field/section]]`, or a block anchor, `[[id#^name]]`. DOC312 checks the whole path and reports an unknown field, section or anchor.
block_anchors: A paragraph, a list item or a one-line field that ends with a space and `^name` gets a block anchor; the name starts with a letter. `[[id#^name]]` links to that paragraph and `{{id#^name}}` includes it without the marker. The page gets an HTML anchor at that place.
A name used twice in one document, or equal to the anchor of a field or section heading of the page, is DOC212, a core rule.
change_tracking: The file `docc.lock` lies next to `docc.json` and is committed. It holds one line per link, sorted: `<source> <target> <targetHash> [<codeHash>]`. The source is a document id or a code file; spaces in a target are written as `%20`. Links in `notes` and in hidden documents are recorded too.

The target hash covers only what the link points to: a block anchor hashes its paragraph, a field or section hashes its value, and a whole document is hashed without `notes`, `docIgnore`, `hidden`, `order`, `parent` and `$comments`, so a reader's comment does not make the links to a document suspect. The code hash exists only for a `docc:begin` region and covers its trimmed text in NFC.

`docc build` without errors records the links that are not in the lock with their hashes, so they count as confirmed, drops the links that are gone and keeps the stored hashes of the rest. Moving a code file confirms nothing: when the file of a region link is gone and, for its target, exactly one region link vanished that way and exactly one appeared, the link that appeared keeps the stored hashes, so a change made along with the move still raises DOC402 (or DOC209); two or more on either side cannot be paired and are recorded with their current hashes. When a target changes after that, DOC209 warns on the source: read it and check that it still agrees. When a code region changes, DOC402 warns: check the document it points to. `docc ack` stores the current hashes of the changed links and clears both warnings; it prints every link it confirms.
`docc check` reports DOC503, a core rule, when `docc.lock` does not match the links in the sources; `docc build` fixes it.
hidden_material: `notes` are for agents and never reach the Markdown.
A document with `hidden` set to `true` is checked like any other, gets no page and cannot be linked from a visible document.
The include `{{id#field}}`, `{{id#field/section}}` or `{{id#^name}}` is replaced at build time by the text it names, so a fact is stored once.
suppression: `docIgnore` lists entries with a rule (its name, such as text/forbidden-words), a mandatory reason and an optional JSON pointer path. Core rules cannot be suppressed or switched off. An entry that suppresses nothing is reported as DOC901.
sections: A free field can hold named sections: an object with the member `"$sections": true`, whose other keys are section titles. A value is text, an array of paragraphs, a list object or another set of sections. It is rendered as a second level heading for the field, third level for a section, and so on up to the sixth, in file order. A section without text keeps its heading, so a link to it has a target.
An object without the marker is rendered as a bullet list. The marker means nothing outside the value of a field or a section.

A section is linked with `[[id#field/section]]`; the link text is the section title, not the title of the document. A section is included with `{{id#field/section}}`; the path is matched against the keys, so a key may contain a slash. The anchor comes from the heading like the anchor of a field; equal anchors on one page are numbered -1, -2 in page order. Text rules and `docIgnore` paths treat sections like fields. A kind schema describes the marker as `"properties": {"$sections": {"const": true}}`.
form_fields: An item of an array of paragraphs (`body`, a free field or a section) can be a form field: `{"$input": "radio", "id": "export", "label": "Export to Excel?", "options": ["Yes", "No"]}`. `$input` is `text` (a text box), `radio` (one choice of two or more options) or `checkbox` (any choices of one or more options); the id is unique in the document and the answers are kept by it; `label` is the question; a text box has no options; no other keys are allowed. A radio or checkbox field also takes an own answer, a text that is none of its options: radio one option or one own text, checkbox the options ticked and at most one own text. DOC112 reports an answer with no value, a blank value or a value given twice, and an answer to the field as it reads now that the field cannot take; an answer to an earlier version of the question is not checked against the field. `docc comments apply` checks the same on add and edit and trims the values that are not options, as the HTML file does. DOC111 reports a malformed field and a field outside an array of paragraphs.

The author writes the fields in the sources, by hand or through an agent; readers answer them in the HTML file ([[rendering]]). The Markdown output leaves them out. In the history a field is a block of its own, so the paragraphs around it keep theirs. Text rules read only the question and the options. The built-in schema allows a field in `body`; a free field holding one needs a kind schema that allows the object.
comments: The top-level member `$comments` holds the readers' comments of the document as a flat list: `[{"id", "at", "quote", "fragment"?, "prefix"?, "suffix"?, "text", "author", "email"?, "created", "edited"?}]`. `id` is unique in the project (docc gives `c-` and ten characters of a-z and 2-7), `at` is the JSON Pointer of a block the reader sees on the page (never notes, `docIgnore`, `hidden`, the title or `$comments`), `quote` the source text of that block when the comment was written (docc fills it from the block, whatever the caller gives), `fragment`, `prefix` and `suffix` the selected words and a few characters around them, `author` a name (it may be empty), `created` an RFC 3339 time and `edited` the RFC 3339 time of the last edit of the text or the answer (docc comments apply edit sets it; add does not). An answer to a form field has `input` (the field id) and `answer` (an array of strings) instead of `text`, and its `at` points at the field.

There are no statuses and no replies: a handled comment is deleted in the same commit as the fix, and a note meant only for agents goes into `notes`. The member is allowed under every kind like `title`, even by a strict kind schema; text rules do not read it, it is no section of the page and no block of the history, and the hash of a whole document in `docc.lock` leaves it out. Only docc writes it, with `docc comments apply` ([[commands]]). DOC112 reports a malformed item or an id used twice in the project; DOC215 warns when a comment lost its place: no block at `at` (a paragraph was inserted, moved or removed above it), the selected words are gone from the block, or the answered field is not there.
